Open — or focus — the browser tab showing one panel.

The window name is keyed on the panel id, so a second click focuses the
existing tab instead of opening a duplicate.

The URL is relative — `panel?id=<panel>`, not `/panel?id=<panel>` — so it
resolves against wherever the app is served from rather than the domain
root.

returns.desc: The panel window, or `null` when the browser blocked it.

sideEffect: Opens a browser window and moves focus to it.

methods.name: openPanelGroupWindow
methods.summary: Open — or focus — a browser tab showing a whole docked window's worth of panels.
methods.description:
Open — or focus — a browser tab showing a whole docked window's worth of panels.

The tab reproduces the group it came from: the same panels, in the same tab
order, with `active` in front.

The window name is keyed on the group's members rather than its order, so
re-popping the same set of panels focuses the tab already showing them
instead of opening a second copy of it.

params.name: ids
params.desc: Panel ids in tab order. An empty list opens nothing.

params.name: active
params.desc: Panel to show first. Defaults to the first id.

returns.desc: The panel window, or `null` when the browser blocked it or the list was empty.

sideEffect: Opens a browser window and moves focus to it.

module.summary: Marquee selection geometry — the arithmetic behind a right-drag lasso on the node editor.
module.description:
Marquee selection geometry — the arithmetic behind a right-drag lasso on the
node editor.

Kept out of the canvas component because it is the part worth being sure
about: a rectangle dragged up-and-left has a negative width, a node that has
never been measured has no size, and "inside the box" is really "overlaps the
box" in every editor users have met. None of that needs React to be checked.

All coordinates here are canvas coordinates, not screen pixels. The caller
converts through React Flow's `screenToFlowPosition` before calling in.

constants.name: MARQUEE_THRESHOLD
constants.summary: Smallest right-drag, in pixels, that counts as a marquee rather than a click.
constants.description:
Smallest right-drag, in pixels, that counts as a marquee rather than a click.

Below this the gesture opens the context menu. Three pixels of travel is
within the slop of a deliberate click on a trackpad, so the threshold sits
just above it.

methods.name: marqueeRect
methods.summary: The axis-aligned rectangle spanned by two corners.
methods.description:
The axis-aligned rectangle spanned by two corners.

A drag may run in any direction, so the corners are sorted rather than
assumed — dragging up-and-left is as ordinary as down-and-right.

params.name: a
params.desc: One corner, where the drag began.

params.name: b
params.desc: The opposite corner, where it is now.

returns.type: {x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number}
returns.desc: The rectangle, with non-negative width and height.

methods.name: nodeBox
methods.summary: A node's bounding box in canvas coordinates.
methods.description:
A node's bounding box in canvas coordinates.

React Flow writes measured dimensions back onto each node once it has been
laid out; until then it falls back to a nominal size so a just-created node
is still catchable.

params.name: node
params.desc: A React Flow node, with `position` and optionally measured `width`/`height`.

returns.type: {x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number}
returns.desc: The node's box.

methods.name: overlaps
methods.summary: Whether two rectangles overlap at all.
methods.description:
Whether two rectangles overlap at all.

Touching edges do not count: a zero-area intersection is what a lasso drawn
exactly along a node's border produces, and catching the node then would be
indistinguishable from a stray click.

params.name: a
params.type: {x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number}

params.name: b
params.type: {x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number}

returns.desc: True when the two overlap.

methods.name: nodesInMarquee
methods.summary: Which nodes a marquee has caught.
methods.description:
Which nodes a marquee has caught.

Overlap rather than containment, matching every drawing tool the user has
met: sweeping across a row of nodes selects them without having to enclose
the last one completely.

params.name: rect
params.type: {x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number}

returns.desc: Ids of the caught nodes, in graph order.

methods.name: distance
methods.summary: How far apart two screen points are, in pixels.
methods.description:
How far apart two screen points are, in pixels.

Used to tell a right-*click* from a right-*drag*: below the threshold the
gesture is a click and must open the context menu instead.

returns.desc: The distance between them.

module.summary: Application state: the project graph, the workspace, and everything the UI reads. One Zustand store, deliberately flat.
module.description:
Application state: the project graph, the workspace, and everything the UI
reads. One Zustand store, deliberately flat.

State fields, since the action contracts below name what changes rather than
where:

  project    nodes, edges, projectName, selectedNodeId, settings
  results    results, metrics, simError
  history    history, future, clipboard
  workspace  layout, layoutPresets, maximized, focusedPanel, draggingPanel,
             poppedOut, toolbar, bindings, xZoom
  modals     showDriverDB, showTSCalc, showSettings, settingsSection,
             workspacePrompt, velocityPopupNodeId

Fields prefixed with an underscore are solver and persistence bookkeeping
(`_lastSig`, `_simToken`, `_computeTimer`, `_flowApi`) and are not part of
any action's observable contract.

LocalStorage keys, all prefixed `acousim:` — `acousim:layout`,
`acousim:layoutPresets`, `acousim:toolbar`, `acousim:keymap`,
`acousim:workspace` and `acousim:workspaceChosen`.

A subset of the state is mirrored to popped-out panel windows over a
BroadcastChannel; see src/popout.js for which keys and why.

constants.name: SNAPSHOT_LIMIT
constants.summary: How many reference overlays a chart will carry.
constants.description:
How many reference overlays a chart will carry.

Three is what stays legible over a live trace; a fourth turns a comparison
into a thicket.

constants.name: SNAPSHOT_COLORS
constants.summary: Overlay colours, chosen to stay apart from the live trace and each other.
constants.description: Overlay colours, chosen to stay apart from the live trace and each other.

methods.name: simulateInWorker
methods.summary: Run one sweep in the simulation worker.
methods.description:
Run one sweep in the simulation worker.

Each request carries an id and resolves its own promise, so several runs may
be in flight without their replies being confused. Replies whose id is no
longer pending are dropped, which is what makes a superseded run harmless.

returns.type: Promise<{id: number, ok: boolean, results?: object, metrics?: object|null, error?: string, projectErrors?: string[]|null}>
returns.desc: The worker's reply.

sideEffect: Spawns the worker on first call and posts a message to it.

methods.name: simWorker.onmessage
methods.summary: Resolve the request a worker reply belongs to.
methods.description:
Resolve the request a worker reply belongs to.

An unrecognised id is dropped rather than treated as an error: it means
the request was superseded and its entry already removed.

params.name: e
params.desc: The reply, carrying the `id` of its request.

sideEffect: Removes the request from `simPending` and resolves its promise.

methods.name: syncPopoutUrl
methods.summary: Rewrite a popped-out tab's own URL to match what it now holds.
methods.description:
Rewrite a popped-out tab's own URL to match what it now holds.

The URL seeds the tab but does not own it: views can be added and closed
once it is open. Keeping the address in step means reloading the tab — or
restoring it after a browser restart — brings back the window the user
actually built rather than the one they first opened.

`replaceState` rather than `pushState`, since adding a view is not somewhere
the back button should return from.

params.name: ids
params.desc: Panel ids the tab now holds, in tab order.

sideEffect: Replaces the current history entry. Silently does nothing where the History API is unavailable.

methods.name: needsStorageChoice
methods.summary: Whether the user has already been asked where their workspace lives.
methods.description:
Whether the user has already been asked where their workspace lives.

A popped-out tab never asks: it owns no workspace of its own and the
question belongs to the window that does.

returns.desc: True when the prompt should be shown.

sideEffect: Reads LocalStorage and the window's own URL.

methods.name: loadWorkspace
methods.summary: Load the persisted workspace, or build a first-run one.
methods.description:
Load the persisted workspace, or build a first-run one.

A workspace that fails to parse is replaced rather than repaired: the file
browser cannot show something it cannot read, and a half-recovered workspace
would be harder to reason about than an empty one.

Custom drivers saved by a build that predates workspaces are adopted into
the new one. That only happens on a genuine first run — an existing
workspace is never modified on load, since the system folder is supposed to
appear when something writes to it, not when the app starts.

returns.desc: A usable workspace.

sideEffect: Reads LocalStorage and the current time.

methods.name: loadLayout
methods.summary: Load the persisted dock layout, falling back to the default.
methods.description:
Load the persisted dock layout, falling back to the default.

Three things can invalidate a stored layout: a version mismatch, a panel
this build no longer has, or corrupt JSON. All three land on the default
rather than throwing. The canvas check is the last guard — a layout
without the Node Editor would leave the workspace with nothing to edit,
so it is rejected even if it is otherwise valid.

returns.desc: A usable layout tree.

sideEffect: Reads LocalStorage.

methods.name: loadPresets
methods.summary: Load the user's saved layout arrangements.
methods.description: Load the user's saved layout arrangements.

returns.desc: Saved presets, or an empty list when absent or corrupt.

sideEffect: Reads LocalStorage.

methods.name: loadToolbar
methods.summary: Load the quick-bar arrangement.
methods.description:
Load the quick-bar arrangement.

It lives in LocalStorage beside the layout rather than in `settings`
because settings travel inside a project file, and opening someone
else's design should not rearrange your toolbar.

returns.desc: Quick-bar item ids, falling back to the default arrangement.

sideEffect: Reads LocalStorage.

methods.name: nextId
methods.summary: Generate a unique node or edge id.
methods.description:
Generate a unique node or edge id.

Combines the node type, the clock and a module counter, so ids stay
unique across a paste that creates several nodes in the same
millisecond, and stay readable in a saved project file.

params.name: type
params.desc: Node type, used as the id's prefix.

returns.desc: A new id, unique within this session.

sideEffect: Advances the module-level counter.

methods.name: freeSpotNear
methods.summary: Find an unoccupied canvas position near a preferred spot.
methods.description:
Find an unoccupied canvas position near a preferred spot.

Adding several elements without moving the mouse would stack them all on
one point, so this steps down-right until the spot is clear.

params.name: nodes
params.desc: Existing nodes, whose positions are avoided.

params.name: step
params.desc: Both the collision radius and the offset per attempt.

params.name: limit
params.desc: Maximum attempts before giving up and returning the last position tried, which may overlap.

returns.desc: A position to place the node at.

post: spot and nodes are not modified

methods.name: taken
methods.summary: Whether any existing node sits within one step of a point.
methods.description: Whether any existing node sits within one step of a point.

returns.desc: True when the spot is occupied.

reads: the enclosing `nodes` list and `step` radius.

methods.name: graphSignature
methods.summary: A value that changes exactly when the simulation would produce a different result.
methods.description:
A value that changes exactly when the simulation would produce a different result.

Used to skip redundant solves. Deliberately excludes everything the
solver ignores — node positions, selection, labels — so dragging a node
around the canvas does not re-run the sweep.

returns.desc: A JSON signature, compared by equality against the last solved one.

methods.name: set
methods.summary: Update state and mirror the shared slice to other windows.
methods.description:
Update state and mirror the shared slice to other windows.

Wraps Zustand's setter so cross-window sync happens in exactly one place
rather than at every call site. Only keys in `SHARED_KEYS` are broadcast,
and only when they were actually touched, so local UI state stays local.

`applyingRemote` suppresses the echo when the update *came from* another
window, and `muted` keeps a freshly opened popout quiet until the main
window has sent it a snapshot — without that, its own start-up writes
would race across the channel and overwrite the project the main window
is showing.

params.name: partial
params.desc: State delta, as Zustand accepts it.

params.name: replace
params.desc: Replace rather than merge the state.

sideEffect: Writes store state and may post a message on the BroadcastChannel.
reads: The module-level `applyingRemote` and `muted` flags.

methods.name: openContextMenu
methods.summary: Open the context menu at a point, against whatever was right-clicked.
methods.description: Open the context menu at a point, against whatever was right-clicked.

params.name: x
params.desc: Viewport x, where the menu's corner goes.

params.name: target
params.desc: What was right-clicked: `{kind: 'pane'|'node'|'edge'|'stack'|'tab', …}` with the ids that kind needs.

sideEffect: Writes store state. The field is local to the window — `SHARED_KEYS` deliberately excludes it, so a right-click does not open a menu in another window.

methods.name: closeContextMenu
methods.summary: Dismiss the context menu.
methods.description:
Dismiss the context menu.

Guarded against redundant writes: closing is attempted on every click
anywhere, and an unconditional write would re-render the workspace on each
one.

sideEffect: Writes store state, when a menu was open.

methods.name: setDraggingPanel
methods.summary: Record which panel is mid tab-drag, which drives the drop targets.
methods.description: Record which panel is mid tab-drag, which drives the drop targets.

params.name: id
params.desc: Panel id, or `null` when the drag ends.

sideEffect: Writes store state. The field is local to the window — `SHARED_KEYS` deliberately excludes it, so a popped-out panel keeps its own.

methods.name: focusPanel
methods.summary: Give a panel keyboard focus, deciding which scoped commands fire.
methods.description:
Give a panel keyboard focus, deciding which scoped commands fire.

Guarded against redundant writes because focus changes on every click and
an unchanged write would still broadcast.

sideEffect: Writes store state. The field is local to the window — `SHARED_KEYS` deliberately excludes it, so a popped-out panel keeps its own.

methods.name: toggleMaximize
methods.summary: Maximize a panel full-bleed, or restore it if it is already maximized.
methods.description: Maximize a panel full-bleed, or restore it if it is already maximized.

sideEffect: Writes store state. The field is local to the window — `SHARED_KEYS` deliberately excludes it, so a popped-out panel keeps its own.

methods.name: setShowSettings
methods.summary: Open or close the settings window, optionally jumping to a section.
methods.description: Open or close the settings window, optionally jumping to a section.

params.name: section
params.desc: Section to select. The current section is kept when omitted.

sideEffect: Writes store state. The field is local to the window — `SHARED_KEYS` deliberately excludes it, so a popped-out panel keeps its own.

methods.name: setSettingsSection
methods.summary: Switch the settings window to a section.
methods.description: Switch the settings window to a section.

sideEffect: Writes store state. The field is local to the window — `SHARED_KEYS` deliberately excludes it, so a popped-out panel keeps its own.

methods.name: setBinding
methods.summary: Replace a command's combos wholesale.
methods.description: Replace a command's combos wholesale.

params.name: combos
params.desc: The command's complete new combo list.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the bindings to LocalStorage.

methods.name: assignBinding
methods.summary: Give a command a combo, taking it from whatever held it before.
methods.description:
Give a command a combo, taking it from whatever held it before.

Assigning a combo steals it, the way most editors behave — silently
leaving two commands on one key is worse than a visible reassignment, and
the caller is told what it took so the UI can say so.

returns.desc: The id of the command the combo was taken from, or `null` when it was free.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the bindings to LocalStorage.

methods.name: removeBinding
methods.summary: Remove one combo from a command, leaving its others in place.
methods.description: Remove one combo from a command, leaving its others in place.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the bindings to LocalStorage.

methods.name: resetBindings
methods.summary: Restore every command to its default combos.
methods.description: Restore every command to its default combos.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the bindings to LocalStorage, which removes the stored overrides entirely.

methods.name: _commitLayout
methods.summary: Adopt a new layout tree and persist it.
methods.description:
Adopt a new layout tree and persist it.

The single write path for the layout, which is why every operation in
`layoutOps` routes through it. A `null` tree — the result of an edit that
would have emptied the workspace — is ignored rather than applied.

sideEffect: Writes store state and LocalStorage. A quota failure is swallowed: the layout simply will not survive a reload.

methods.name: activate
methods.summary: Bring a panel to the front of its stack.
methods.description: Bring a panel to the front of its stack.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the layout.

methods.name: dock
methods.summary: Move a panel onto a target stack.
methods.description: Move a panel onto a target stack.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the layout.

methods.name: dockEdge
methods.summary: Dock a panel against an outer edge of the workspace.
methods.description: Dock a panel against an outer edge of the workspace.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the layout.

methods.name: resize
methods.summary: Apply a splitter drag, reweighting two adjacent children.
methods.description: Apply a splitter drag, reweighting two adjacent children.

params.name: index
params.desc: Index of the child before the splitter.

params.name: b
params.desc: New weight for the next one.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the layout.

methods.name: dropOnTab
methods.summary: Handle a tab dropped onto another tab.
methods.description:
Handle a tab dropped onto another tab.

Two different operations share one gesture: dropping within the panel's
own stack reorders it, dropping from elsewhere tabs it in. A drop on its
own current position does nothing.

params.name: index
params.desc: Tab position it was dropped at.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the layout.

methods.name: close
methods.summary: Close a panel.
methods.description:
Close a panel.

Panels marked `closable: false` — the canvas, which is the workspace
itself — are refused, as is a close that would empty the layout.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the layout.

methods.name: open
methods.summary: Show a panel and give it focus, docking it if it is not already open.
methods.description:
Show a panel and give it focus, docking it if it is not already open.

Un-maximizes first, since opening a panel behind a maximized one would
otherwise appear to do nothing.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the layout.

methods.name: toggle
methods.summary: Open a panel, or close it if it is already open. Drives the View menu's checkmarks.
methods.description: Open a panel, or close it if it is already open. Drives the View menu's checkmarks.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the layout.

methods.name: reset
methods.summary: Restore the default workspace arrangement.
methods.description: Restore the default workspace arrangement.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the layout.

methods.name: saveLayoutPreset
methods.summary: Save the current arrangement under a name, replacing any preset with that name.
methods.description: Save the current arrangement under a name, replacing any preset with that name.

sideEffect: Writes store state and LocalStorage. A quota failure is swallowed.

methods.name: applyLayoutPreset
methods.summary: Apply a saved arrangement.
methods.description:
Apply a saved arrangement.

The preset is sanitized before use — it may name panels a later build
dropped — and the canvas is docked back in if sanitizing removed it, so a
stale preset can never leave the workspace without its editor.

params.name: name
params.desc: Preset name. An unknown name is ignored.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the layout.

methods.name: setToolbar
methods.summary: Replace the quick-bar arrangement.
methods.description:
Replace the quick-bar arrangement.

Sanitized on the way in, so an arrangement carrying unknown ids falls
back to the default rather than rendering a broken bar. Unknown ids are
dropped individually; the fallback fires only when nothing survives, since
a non-empty request sanitizing to nothing means the whole arrangement was
foreign. An explicitly empty `ids` is honoured — that is a deliberately
hidden bar, not corruption.

params.name: ids
params.desc: Item ids in display order. A non-array falls back to the default.

sideEffect: Writes store state and LocalStorage. A quota failure is swallowed.

methods.name: toggleToolbarItem
methods.summary: Add an item to the quick bar, or remove it if it is already there.
methods.description:
Add an item to the quick bar, or remove it if it is already there.

Newly added items go to the end rather than their registry position, so
toggling one on does not reshuffle the bar.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the toolbar.

methods.name: moveToolbarItem
methods.summary: Move an item along the quick bar by swapping it with its neighbour.
methods.description: Move an item along the quick bar by swapping it with its neighbour.

params.name: delta
params.desc: Positions to move by; -1 is left, 1 is right.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the toolbar. Does nothing when the item is absent or the move would run off either end.

methods.name: resetToolbar
methods.summary: Restore the default quick-bar arrangement.
methods.description: Restore the default quick-bar arrangement.

sideEffect: Writes store state and persists the toolbar, since it delegates to `setToolbar`. The toolbar is local to the window; `SHARED_KEYS` excludes it.

methods.name: deleteLayoutPreset
methods.summary: Delete a saved arrangement.
methods.description: Delete a saved arrangement.

sideEffect: Writes store state and LocalStorage.

methods.name: setXZoom
methods.summary: Store one chart's X-axis zoom range, set by drag-selecting on the plot.
methods.description:
Store one chart's X-axis zoom range, set by drag-selecting on the plot.

Not persisted: zoom is a transient view of the current result.

sideEffect: Writes store state, mirrored to other windows.

methods.name: pushHistory
methods.summary: Record the current graph as an undo point.
methods.description:
Record the current graph as an undo point.

Called before a mutation rather than after, so the entry is the state to
return *to*. Deep-copies nodes and edges, since undo must not hand back
objects a later edit has since mutated. Pushing clears the redo stack,
which is the standard linear-history behaviour.

sideEffect: Writes store state. The history is capped at 80 entries, oldest discarded.

methods.name: undo
methods.summary: Step back one entry in the history.
methods.description: Step back one entry in the history.

sideEffect: Writes store state and schedules a resimulation. Does nothing when the history is empty.

methods.name: redo
methods.summary: Step forward one entry in the history.
methods.description: Step forward one entry in the history.

sideEffect: Writes store state and schedules a resimulation. Does nothing when the redo stack is empty.

methods.name: onNodesChange
methods.summary: Apply React Flow's node changes — drags, selections, removals.
methods.description:
Apply React Flow's node changes — drags, selections, removals.

Only removals schedule a resimulation: moving or selecting a node cannot
change the result, and re-solving on every frame of a drag would be
wasteful. Note that this does not push history, because it fires
continuously during a drag.

sideEffect: Writes store state, and schedules a resimulation when a node was removed.

methods.name: onEdgesChange
methods.summary: Apply React Flow's edge changes.
methods.description:
Apply React Flow's edge changes.

Removals push history and schedule a resimulation, since deleting an edge
changes the topology.

sideEffect: Writes store state, and on removal records history and schedules a resimulation.

methods.name: onConnect
methods.summary: Add an edge from a completed port-to-port drag.
methods.description: Add an edge from a completed port-to-port drag.

params.name: conn
params.desc: React Flow connection: source, sourceHandle, target, targetHandle.

sideEffect: Records history, writes store state and schedules a resimulation.

methods.name: setSelected
methods.summary: Select a node, which drives what the Parameters panel edits.
methods.description: Select a node, which drives what the Parameters panel edits.

sideEffect: Writes store state, mirrored to other windows.

methods.name: addNode
methods.summary: Add a node of the given type at a canvas position.
methods.description:
Add a node of the given type at a canvas position.

The new node arrives selected — and alone in the selection — so it can be
copied, nudged or deleted straight away without clicking it first.

params.name: type
params.desc: Node type; its entry in `DEFAULT_PARAMS` supplies the initial params.

returns.desc: The new node's id, so callers can immediately update its params.

sideEffect: Records history, writes store state and schedules a resimulation.

methods.name: updateParams
methods.summary: Merge a patch into one node's parameters.
methods.description: Merge a patch into one node's parameters.

params.name: id
params.desc: Node id. An unknown id is a no-op.

params.name: patch
params.desc: Parameters to merge over the node's existing ones.

sideEffect: Writes store state and schedules a resimulation.

methods.name: deleteSelected
methods.summary: Delete the selected nodes and edges.
methods.description:
Delete the selected nodes and edges.

Edges attached to a deleted node go with it, whether or not they were
themselves selected — leaving a dangling edge would corrupt the graph.

sideEffect: Records history, writes store state and schedules a resimulation. Does nothing when the selection is empty.

methods.name: duplicateSelected
methods.summary: Copy the selected nodes in place, offset down-right.
methods.description:
Copy the selected nodes in place, offset down-right.

Deep-copies each node's params so the duplicate is independent, and moves
the selection to the copies — matching the usual expectation that what
you just created is what you are now holding. Edges are not duplicated;
`copySelection` and `pasteClipboard` are the path that preserves them.

sideEffect: Records history, writes store state and schedules a resimulation. Does nothing when the selection is empty.

methods.name: selectAll
methods.summary: Select every node on the canvas.
methods.description: Select every node on the canvas.

sideEffect: Writes store state, mirrored to other windows.

methods.name: setSelection
methods.summary: Replace — or extend — the node selection.
methods.description:
Replace — or extend — the node selection.

The write path for the right-drag marquee. `selectedNodeId`, which is what
the Parameters panel edits, follows the last node in the new selection, so
lassoing a group leaves something concrete to edit rather than an empty
panel. An empty selection clears it.

params.name: additive
params.desc: Keep the existing selection and add to it, which is what a modifier-held lasso means.

sideEffect: Writes store state, mirrored to other windows. Does not record history — selection is not an edit.

methods.name: copySelection
methods.summary: Copy the selected nodes and their internal edges to the in-app clipboard.
methods.description:
Copy the selected nodes and their internal edges to the in-app clipboard.

An in-app clipboard rather than the system one: the graph is a structure,
not text, and reading the system clipboard needs a permission prompt on
every paste. It rides the sync channel, so you can copy in the main
window and paste into a popped-out Node Editor.

Only edges wholly inside the selection are taken — a dangling half-edge
would have nothing to reconnect to on paste.

An empty selection leaves the previous clipboard in place rather than
clearing it, so a stray copy with nothing selected cannot lose what you
copied a moment ago. There is no action that empties the clipboard.

returns.desc: How many nodes were copied; 0 when the selection was empty.

sideEffect: Writes store state, mirrored to other windows.

methods.name: cutSelection
methods.summary: Copy the selection, then delete it.
methods.description:
Copy the selection, then delete it.

Deletes only if the copy found something, so an empty selection cannot
delete anything.

sideEffect: Records history, writes store state and schedules a resimulation.

methods.name: pasteClipboard
methods.summary: Paste the clipboard as new nodes, at a point or offset down-right.
methods.description:
Paste the clipboard as new nodes, at a point or offset down-right.

Every pasted node gets a fresh id, and the copied edges are rewired
through a remap table so they connect the copies rather than the
originals. Params are merged over the current defaults, so pasting into a
newer build fills in any parameter added since the copy was made.

methods.name: scheduleCompute
methods.summary: Schedule a debounced simulation run.
methods.description:
Schedule a debounced simulation run.

Simulation runs in a Web Worker — see `src/engine/worker.js` — so the
canvas stays responsive through a large sweep, and three mechanisms keep
the pipeline from thrashing. The 150 ms debounce collapses slider drags
into one run. The graph signature skips the run when nothing that affects
the result changed. A token marks the newest request, and the reply is
checked against it before being applied, so a slow reply cannot overwrite
a newer result.

A superseded run is left to finish rather than cancelled. Tearing down and
respawning a worker costs more than the sweep it would save, and the reply
is discarded either way.

A popped-out tab returns immediately: results arrive from the main window
over the sync channel, and a second sweep would duplicate the work.

methods.name: useBackdropDismiss
methods.summary: Props for a modal backdrop that dismisses on a click, but not on a drag that merely finished over it.
methods.description:
Props for a modal backdrop that dismisses on a click, but not on a drag
that merely finished over it.

A bare `onClick` on the backdrop is wrong, and wrong in a way that only
shows up once there is text worth selecting. `click` fires on the nearest
common ancestor of where the button went down and where it came up, so
pressing inside a text field, sweeping past the dialog's edge and
releasing lands a click on the backdrop itself — a selection gesture that
throws the dialog away mid-edit. Stopping propagation inside the dialog
cannot help: the event was never dispatched there to begin with.

So both ends of the gesture are checked instead, on the press and on the
release, and the dialog is dismissed only when neither touched it. That
also rules out the mirror case — pressing on the backdrop and releasing
inside the dialog, which is how a user drags a selection the other way.

The arming flag is a ref rather than a closure variable because React may
re-render between the press and the release, which would otherwise hand
the second handler a fresh, unarmed copy.

Because both ends are checked against `currentTarget`, the dialog this
wraps needs no `onClick` of its own to shield itself.

params.name: close
params.desc: Called when the backdrop is genuinely clicked.

returns.desc: Props to spread onto the backdrop element.

sideEffect: Allocates a ref on the calling component.

methods.summary: Arm the dismissal only if the press landed on the backdrop itself.
methods.description: Arm the dismissal only if the press landed on the backdrop itself.

mutates: the arming ref.

methods.name: onMouseUp
methods.summary: Dismiss, if this release and the press that began it were both on the backdrop.

module.summary: A minimal ZIP reader and writer.
module.description:
A minimal ZIP reader and writer.

Written by hand rather than pulled from a package because the whole of what
is needed here is one archive shape: a flat list of paths, each holding a
small JSON document. That is a few hundred lines of well-documented format,
against a dependency in a project that otherwise has none for this.

Compression is the browser's. `CompressionStream('deflate-raw')` and its
decompressing twin are built in, which leaves this module responsible only
for the container — headers, the central directory, and the CRC. Where the
streams are unavailable, entries are stored uncompressed; a ZIP with stored
entries is still a perfectly ordinary ZIP.

Deliberately not supported: encryption, ZIP64, multi-disk archives, and the
compression methods older than deflate. An archive using any of them is
rejected by name rather than half-read. Workspaces are tens of kilobytes of
JSON, so the 4 GB and 65,535-entry ceilings that ZIP64 exists to lift are
not ceilings this will meet.

module.summary: The workspace model: a user's projects, folders and app data as one self-contained, downloadable object.
module.description:
The workspace model: a user's projects, folders and app data as one
self-contained, downloadable object.

A workspace is deliberately flat. Files are held in a map keyed by path
rather than in a nested tree, because every interesting operation — write,
rename, delete, "does this exist" — is a single map lookup on a path, while
the same operations on a tree are recursive walks that have to rebuild the
spine. The tree the file browser draws is *derived*, once, at render time.

Folders are implied by the paths of the files inside them, which means a
folder normally needs no record of its own. Empty folders are the exception:
a user who makes a folder and has not yet put anything in it would otherwise
watch it vanish, so those are listed explicitly and pruned as files arrive.

One folder is special. `.acousim` holds data the app itself tracks rather
than data the user authored — custom drivers today, more as features land.
It is created lazily and never eagerly: an imported workspace that predates
the folder, or one a user has trimmed by hand, stays exactly as imported
until something actually needs to write there. Creating it on import would
modify a workspace the user only meant to open.

Nothing here touches storage or the DOM. Persistence, downloading and the
current time all belong to the caller; these are value-to-value functions so
that "what does renaming a folder do" can be answered without a browser.

Driver-library integrity checks.

The library is large enough now that a bad row would hide rather than
announce itself, and a driver whose parameters disagree with each other
produces a plausible-looking simulation of nothing real.

Two tiers. Hard checks are identities the loader controls — the schema, and
the Cms/Rms the importer derives — and must hold exactly. The audit tier
covers published values that can legitimately disagree with each other in a
real catalog; those rows are permitted, but only if they carry a `suspect`
label, so the count can never grow silently.

from tests.

The contract suite needs to reach helpers that happen to live beside React
components — the T/S solvers in TSCalc.jsx, the axis-fitting maths in
OutputPanel.jsx — and Node cannot parse JSX. esbuild is already in the tree
as a Vite dependency, so this transforms on the fly rather than adding a
build step or a test-only dependency.
